'''Kaonism''' is a moderate collectivist ideology that old source material presents as a philosophical predecessor to political [[Taoism]]. It emerged in the [[Imperial Dynasty of Saochai|Saochi/Saochai]] political world during the mid-nineteenth century.

Kaonism argued that hierarchy should be ethically transformed rather than destroyed. It emphasized moral statecraft, restrained authority, communal stewardship of essential resources, ritualized reform, and balance between labor, law, nature, and public duty.

== Origins ==

Kaonism developed during the [[Saochian Reorganization Period]], roughly 1841-1863. The period was marked by famine, weakening agrarian traditions, urban unrest, and fractured governance.

Its founder, [[Liao Zhengyuan]], was a low-ranking scholar and civil administrator. His major works, ''The Bond of People'' in 1844 and ''Measure of the Self-State'' in 1848, proposed collective stewardship, rotating civic leadership, moral training for officials, and ritualized reform instead of violent revolution.

The movement circulated among reformist literati, provincial cooperatives, and guild circles, but it did not become a mass party in Saochi.

== Doctrine ==

Kaonism's central idea was harmony through disciplined reform. It opposed exploitative hierarchy but did not reject hierarchy itself. Leaders were expected to govern with restraint, spiritual clarity, and accountability to the social whole.

Economically, Kaonism favored collective management of core land and industries without total leveling of society. It treated ownership as stewardship and warned that violent redistribution could damage the social rhythm it wanted to protect.

Politically, Kaonism favored gradual institutional change, civic training, seasonal councils, and moralized bureaucracy. It rejected chaos and populist violence, but also rejected aristocratic decay and industrial cruelty.

== Suppression And Exile ==

Kaonist texts were banned during the [[Purge of 1865]]. Liao was arrested and disappeared soon after, with the source treating him as presumed dead in exile.

Surviving adherents moved eastward into borderlands and industrial communities. There, Kaonist concepts entered broader reform circles and eventually influenced the political language later associated with Taoism.

== Relationship With Taoism ==

Old source material says Kaonism became a quiet ancestor of modern Taoism, especially through ideas such as moralized governance, the Fourfold Alignment, non-revolutionary collectivism, and ritual leadership.

The same source names a Taoist synthesizer as Xing Tao. Existing AGGSWorld drafts use [[Xun Tao]] as the central Xanaq Taoist revolutionary figure. This draft routes the influence to the existing Xun Tao/Taoism chain while flagging the name variant for review.
